diagnostic_evidence.quote: In the stiff limit, backward Euler is $L$-stable and acts as a projection onto the local equilibrium manifold, yielding a strongly AP scheme.
A complete AP analysis of the fully nonlinear coupled system would require accounting for errors in the macroscopic field solver, which is beyond the scope of this work.
If the electric field is spatially constant (even if large), we may choose $\bar{\beta}=\beta_p$

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract, introduction and conclusion advertise a proof of the AP property, and Section 5 asserts a 'strongly AP scheme'. What is actually proved is weaker. Theorem thm:main_AP is a single-step relaxation bound with the field frozen. Its error term proportional to kappa_h does not vanish as eps->0, and it holds only under the formal assumption ||G||=O(1). No consistency of the limiting scheme with the macroscopic drift system (eq:macro_drift) is shown, and the coupled-field analysis is explicitly deferred. The 'small fluctuation' regime is also nearly empty. With beta_p=exp(-dv E_p/2), kappa_h is about 2||E-mean E||_inf/dv. By contrast, gamma_h is O(M_min/L_v^2), with M_min about e^{-18} on [-6,6]. So asm:small_fluct requires the field fluctuation to be about 1e-9*dv or smaller, and fails under mesh refinement for any nonconstant field. Even when it holds, the kappa_h-term in eq:distance_bound is O(1) relative to ||rho M|| unless kappa_h*M_max is much smaller than gamma_h. With periodic x and E=-phi_x, a spatially constant field must vanish, so the 'even if large' strong-AP case is just E=0.

failure_location.quote: For the first-order scheme, we prove an asymptotic-preserving (AP) property when the field fluctuation is small.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the abstract, introduction, Section 5 opening and conclusion to claim only a one-step relaxation estimate toward the local Maxwellian with frozen field, conditional on ||G||=O(1). This bound is exact only for E constant (E=0 in the periodic setting). Drop the 'strongly AP' assertion unless a limiting-scheme consistency analysis is added.
issues.overall_effect: The headline theoretical guarantee (AP of the first-order low-rank scheme) is not established. Only an O(eps)+O(kappa_h/gamma_h) one-step relaxation estimate under a nearly vacuous condition is proved.
issues.title: Claimed AP proof exceeds what Theorem thm:main_AP establishes
issues.why_classification: The formal content survives, but an advertised guarantee must be materially weakened from AP to partial relaxation under an essentially degenerate regime. This is a limited but real loss, short of abandoning a result.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\bar{u}$ denote the spatial vector of arithmetic means

issues.failure_explanation: The bound |ū|^2 <= L_v M_max ||u-ū||^2 is derived for the scalar mean ū. However, ||ū||_v^h, the v-norm of a constant, equals sqrt(L_v)|ū|. The written chain therefore gives (1+L_v sqrt(M_max))^2, not (1+sqrt(L_v M_max))^2. For L_v=12 the claimed gamma_h is larger than the argument supports. The stated constant is recovered only with the sharper bound ||M||^2 <= M_max<M,1> = M_max, which the proof does not use.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ||M||^2 <= L_v M_max by ||M||^2 <= M_max (using the normalization <M,1>=1). Then |ū| <= sqrt(M_max)||u-ū|| and ||ū||_v^h <= sqrt(L_v M_max)||u-ū||, which restores the stated gamma_h.
issues.overall_effect: The value of gamma_h, as stated, is unproved. Through gamma_h, this propagates to Assumption asm:small_fluct and to the constants in Theorem thm:main_AP.
issues.title: Coercivity proof conflates |ū| with its v-norm; stated constant not supported by written chain
issues.why_classification: A one-line local correction restores the exact stated constant and all downstream statements.

issues.failure_explanation: With the stated symmetric second-difference operators, beta*T^(alpha) + beta^{-1}*T^(1/alpha) gives coefficient beta*alpha_{q+1/2} + 1/(beta*alpha_{q+1/2}) on f_{q+1}. The stencil eq:fp_discrete_separable has only alpha_{q+1/2}*beta_p, so the decomposition is false. The stated operators also have norm up to about 4*alpha_max/dv^2 (e.g. for w_q=(-1)^q), so the claimed bound 2*alpha_max/dv^2 fails for them. The correct one-sided operators read off from the stencil do satisfy the 2*alpha_max/dv^2 bound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define T^(alpha)w_q=(alpha_{q+1/2}w_{q+1}-alpha_{q-1/2}w_q)/dv^2 and T^(1/alpha)w_q=(w_{q-1}/alpha_{q-1/2}-w_q/alpha_{q+1/2})/dv^2, with zero-flux boundary rows. Then bound each by two diagonal-shift terms.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the kappa_h bound is invalid as written. Theorem thm:main_AP uses this bound.
issues.title: Wrong tensor decomposition of L_h and unsupported operator-norm bounds in fluctuation estimate
issues.why_classification: A local redefinition matching the stencil restores the proof with the same constant kappa_h.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof bounds ||M u|| and ||rho M|| using M_max^{n+1}, which requires M_max >= max_{p,q} M_{p,q} over grid nodes. The defined M_max^{n+1} is the maximum of the geometric means M_{p,q+1/2}, which is strictly smaller than the nodal peak in general. For example, take g=(2a,-a,-a) at the peak node and its two neighbours, with neighbour ratio c in (1/2,1). This g satisfies <g,1>=0 and ||g||^2/||g/M||^2 = 3c^2/(2c^2+1)*M*^2 > c*M*^2 = (M_max^{n+1})^2. So the inequality fails, and Assumption asm:small_fluct is weaker than what the absorption step needs.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define M_max^{n+1} as the maximum over grid nodes (which dominates the half-point values). Use this M_max^{n+1} consistently in Assumption asm:small_fluct, Theta and the bounds.
issues.overall_effect: The estimates eq:residual_bound and eq:distance_bound and the absorption argument are not justified with the stated M_max and assumption.
issues.title: M_max defined over half-grid geometric means but used to bound nodal M
issues.why_classification: Redefining one constant (slightly strengthening the assumption) fixes every step without changing the argument or the form of the result.
